action: Follow Unit 42's guidance: tighten identity hygiene (strong unique passwords, no shared or default credentials), cut internet-facing attack surface, patch dated public flaws, and add the two published IP indicators to monitoring.
exec: AI-run intrusions got in through weak passwords, open cloud storage and login bypasses, not new exploits; basic identity and patch upkeep is the defence.
plain: Unit 42 says a likely China-linked group used an AI hacking tool to run 25 mostly automated break-in attempts on at least 19 chip, defence and civil-society bodies, got into 10 and accessed more than one million union member records.

key_findings: Targets were 7 semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing firms, 3 defence or defence-policy bodies and 4 human-rights or civil-society groups, including a Canadian rights body and a US teachers' union.
The cluster ran 25 operations against at least 19 organisations and reached confirmed unauthorised access or data retrieval at 10 of them.
It used a customised fork of the open-source Cairn framework driven by Zhipu GLM 5.2 and DeepSeek V4 models, plus a custom skill pack not in upstream Cairn.
Entry came from password spraying, brute-forced credentials, unauthenticated cloud-storage writes, login bypasses and open registration endpoints rather than new exploits.

At a US teachers' union the framework logged access to more than one million member records, roughly 31,000 CRM contacts and staff password hashes; Unit 42 assesses China-nexus collection with moderate confidence.
recommendations: Tighten identity hygiene: remove weak, default and shared passwords on internet-facing applications.
Reduce the exposed attack surface, including open registration endpoints and unauthenticated cloud storage.
Patch software affected by older public CVEs.
Monitor for the two IP addresses Unit 42 published for the Cairn hosting and staging servers.

summary: Unit 42 tracked a cluster, CL-STA-1238, running a customised fork of the open-source Cairn AI penetration-testing framework on Chinese AI models. It ran 25 operations against at least 19 organisations in the semiconductor supply chain, defence and civil society, with confirmed access or data retrieval at 10. At a US teachers' union it logged access to more than one million member records. Unit 42 assesses China-nexus intelligence collection with moderate confidence.
title: Unit 42: autonomous 'Cairn' operations hit semiconductor, defense and civil-society targets

validation.note: Primary source: the Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 report (12 Nov), re-read on 22 Nov with no update note; AgentBeam timeline tracker removed from sources.

review.note: Compared 25 ops/19 orgs/10 accessed, over 1M records, moderate-confidence China-nexus, models, IPs, date 12 Nov against the Unit 42 report.
